questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How the Black-Scholes model won its creators a Nobel Prize in 1997
The founding, leveraged strategies and 1998 near-collapse of hedge fund LTCM
The history of Salomon Brothers' bond desk and Meriwether's resignation
The rules of the Investment Company Act of 1940 on mutual funds
questions.explain: The passage describes how LTCM was founded, how it traded, how it used leverage, and its 1998 bailout.

questions.q: Why did Meriwether choose to start a hedge fund?
options: To keep its trades secret from Bear Stearns and Merrill Lynch
To raise money exclusively from celebrities and sports figures
To avoid regulation that applied to vehicles like mutual funds
To qualify for direct central bank funding during crises
questions.explain: He chose a hedge fund to avoid the financial regulation imposed on traditional vehicles such as mutual funds.

questions.q: What was LTCM's core trade in Treasury bonds?
options: Buy the newly issued 30-year benchmark and short the older bond
Buy the old benchmark bond and short the newly issued 30-year benchmark
Buy Japanese government bonds and short every UK gilt outstanding
Buy S&P 500 equity options and short Treasuries of similar maturity
questions.explain: LTCM bought the old 29.75-year bond and sold short the newly issued 30-year benchmark that traded at a premium.

questions.q: What was LTCM's debt-to-equity ratio at the start of 1998?
options: About 5 to 1
Over 25 to 1
About 10 to 1
Over 100 to 1
questions.explain: With $4.7 billion in equity and over $124.5 billion borrowed, the ratio was over 25 to 1.

questions.q: Why did LTCM need so much leverage?
options: Regulators required hedge funds to borrow against client capital
Its investors demanded large loans as a condition of their stakes
Price gaps in its trades were tiny, so returns had to be magnified
Bear Stearns charged high fees that only leverage could cover
questions.explain: The passage says valuation discrepancies were only a few basis points, so leverage was needed to earn significant returns.
